description: The production Hosted path for server-verified GitHub identity, first-organization creation, mandatory initial WebAuthn registration, and subsequent human authentication/step-up.

authority_must_not_be_enabled_until: the bootstrap state and idempotency records are durable in PostgreSQL
the bootstrap WebAuthn ceremony is bound to the verified member and organization
the focused contract validator and the real PostgreSQL qualification are green

authority.subject_format: GitHub numeric user id returned by the server-side /user API after OAuth code exchange
subject_verification: the browser is redirected to GitHub with a server-created state and PKCE challenge
the callback validates the one-time state and exact configured redirect URI
the server exchanges the code at GitHub; a browser-supplied access token is never accepted
the server calls GitHub /user with the exchanged token and takes only the verified numeric id
the provider subject is bound to provider=github and an immutable upstream_identities row
authority.web_authn_authority: existing strict WebAuthn verifier and durable challenge coordinator, with bootstrap-session binding
forbidden_identity_sources: caller-supplied GitHub subject, email, member_id, organization_id, or role
Authorization headers or generic bearer tokens
the legacy agentpass-console-identity assertion as Hosted first-sign-in authority

data_model_binding.compatibility_note: The current ordinary Human Session and WebAuthn registration routes require an organization-bound session. The bootstrap implementation therefore needs a separate short-lived bootstrap-session/challenge adapter that uses the same members, organizations, memberships, WebAuthn verifier, and PostgreSQL transaction authority; it must not weaken the existing routes.

membership_decisions.new_user: Create one member and one immutable upstream_identities(provider=github, subject) mapping inside the server transaction; the caller cannot select either identifier.
membership_decisions.existing_user_with_active_membership: Do not create an organization. Resolve the active membership from PostgreSQL and continue through the normal session or WebAuthn step-up path.
membership_decisions.existing_user_with_zero_memberships: Allow exactly one first-organization bootstrap; this includes an existing identity row whose member has never had a membership.
membership_decisions.existing_user_with_revoked_membership_hi: A revoked membership history is not a first organization. Return no_membership and require an invitation or the existing recovery boundary.
membership_decisions.multiple_active_memberships: Never choose an organization from the request. Return a server-derived organization selection state, and require a later organization-bound session.
membership_decisions.caller_role: Always ignored; the first membership is server-created as owner and all later roles come from PostgreSQL.

routes.authority: public entrypoint; no identity is accepted from the request

headers: Origin is not used as OAuth provider authority

response.redirect: the configured GitHub authorization URL with server-generated state, PKCE challenge, exact client_id, and exact redirect_uri

security: state is one-use and stored server-side as a hash
PKCE verifier is stored server-side and never returned to the browser
no GitHub token or subject is placed in the redirect URL

headers: provider redirect; Origin may be absent

response.success_redirect: configured HTTPS Console onboarding path with no query or fragment

security: state, code, redirect URI, PKCE, and GitHub API response are verified server-side
the OAuth state cookie is cleared on every terminal callback
raw GitHub access tokens, emails, names, and raw provider responses never cross the response boundary

routes.authority: server-side bootstrap attempt selected by opaque cookie

headers: Origin must equal the configured HTTPS Console origin

security: safe read may bootstrap the CSRF token; every state-changing route still requires the CSRF header
the response contains no provider subject, member id, role, or bearer

transaction: lock and re-read the bootstrap attempt and upstream identity
prove that the member has zero membership rows, not merely zero active rows
create organization and owner membership with createOrganizationWithOwner
persist the exact idempotency request hash and public response atomically
transition the bootstrap attempt to webauthn_required
security: organization_id, member_id, membership_id, and owner role are never accepted from the caller
concurrent same-intent requests converge to one organization
a different name under the same key is a conflict
a second organization is rejected after the first commit

routes.authority: bootstrap attempt plus server-derived member and organization

requirements: challenge bound to bootstrap attempt, member, organization, and registration operation

transaction: verify user presence and user verification at the configured rp_id and origin
insert the public credential bound to the server-derived member
mark onboarding complete and issue a normal Human Session
security: no normal privileged session is issued before this succeeds
credential public key is never returned as a browser authority token
replayed, cross-member, cross-organization, stale, or wrong-origin assertions fail closed

subsequent_authentication.identity: GitHub OAuth may establish the server-side human identity again; it never selects a member, organization, or role.

allowed_for: credential registration after the first credential
required_for: sensitive organization/member/security mutations according to their existing recent-auth contracts
webauthn.replay_policy: durable consume-once challenge and credential counter/clone checks

transport.console_origin: exact configured HTTPS origin; trailing slash and null are rejected

csrf.source: opaque token returned by bootstrap status and hashed server-side

cookies.name: __Host-agentpass_session
cookies.purpose: ordinary Human Session after WebAuthn gate

transport.cache_policy: no-store, no-cache, and no-store-compatible response headers on all bootstrap responses

idempotency.oauth_state: one-use; every terminal callback consumes and clears it
idempotency.bootstrap_session: single onboarding attempt; rotate or expire after completion

organization_create.same_key_same_body: return the original public organization result without a second write
organization_create.concurrent_same_intent: one owner membership and one organization; all callers converge
organization_create.response_loss: retry with the same key returns the committed public result

recovery_boundary.bootstrap: If the bootstrap cookie is lost before completion, restart GitHub OAuth. No support or browser-supplied identifier may resume an attempt.
recovery_boundary.github_account: GitHub account recovery is outside AgentPass; GitHub email, display name, and organization membership are never used as an authority substitute.
recovery_boundary.post_onboarding: After a credential exists, use the existing owner recovery flow. Recovery may restore a verified human session but may not create a new first organization or silently grant a role.
forbidden: reusing an expired or consumed OAuth state or WebAuthn challenge

migration_compatibility.read_policy: During the compatibility window, resolve GitHub identities from upstream_identities and preserve the legacy members.github_subject mapping for existing rows; never silently reassign an immutable provider subject.
migration_compatibility.write_policy: New writes are canonical provider=github upstream_identities rows in the same transaction as member/organization ownership. The legacy column is compatibility data only and is never a caller input.
migration_compatibility.schema_policy: v1 is exact at every request boundary: unknown request fields are rejected, no field is repurposed, and no old ChatGPT/signed-console route is aliased to this flow.
migration_compatibility.forward_only_requirement: After the identity invalidation boundary in 0056, add the bootstrap attempt, one-use OAuth state, bootstrap idempotency, and bootstrap challenge bindings through forward migration 0057, then add exact state-hash claim and an AEAD-protected PKCE envelope through forward migration 0058 before Hosted activation; do not mutate historical migration files.
migration_compatibility.rollback_policy: Application rollback must leave the forward migration and immutable identity rows intact. A version that cannot understand this contract must fail closed and must not create an organization.
migration_compatibility.versioning: Security or authority changes require v2 and a new contract id; documentation-only clarifications may update the validator without changing v1 semantics.

audit_requirements: identity verified or rejected with provider, subject digest, and outcome only
bootstrap attempt created, expired, or completed
first organization committed or idempotently replayed
WebAuthn challenge issued, consumed, rejected, or replayed
normal Human Session issued or denied
audit records contain no raw OAuth code, access token, subject, cookie, CSRF token, assertion, or credential public key
